name: T-cars Fleet
description: Reads vehicles, people, groups and the journey log from the T-cars SOAP WebService v2 and promotes them onto the raw signal lane. Optional by construction: a deployment without a T-cars contract simply does not install it.
author: Evymo

apiUrl.description: SOAP WebService v2 endpoint (rpc/ENCODED). The WSDL lives at the same URL with ?wsdl.

cisloSmlouvy.description: Contract number — the first field of the tLoginData struct; also the deploy gate for this connector.

codebookSyncCron.description: Vehicles/people/groups are reference data, not a stream: daily is enough.

rideSyncCron.description: The journey log is queried per vehicle, so cost scales with fleet size: hourly during the working day, not at night. Nothing is lost overnight — the next window starts at the stored cursor.

rideOverlapHours.description: Every tick re-reads this many hours before the cursor, so a ride still open at the previous tick is stored complete. Costs rows, not vendor calls.

rideReconcileOverlapHours.description: Once a day the window reaches this far back, to pick up rides the vendor edited after the fact (private/business, corrected distance).

rideReconcileEveryHours.description: How often the long overlap runs; with the default schedule that is the first tick of the day.

projectionWindowMin.description: Rides touched by sync within this many minutes are re-offered to the twin projection, which writes only the ones that actually changed.

rideBackfillDays.description: Window used on the FIRST run only; afterwards the stored cursor decides, so history is never re-read.

ridePauseMs.description: Pause between per-vehicle journey-log calls. Courtesy toward the vendor's production system, not our own throttling.

rideCallBudget.description: Hard ceiling on vendor calls per tick (0 = none). A grown fleet or a misread cursor must not turn one tick into hundreds of requests; when the ceiling stops a run the cursor is held back, so the window is retried rather than skipped.
